caution: These paraphrased published descriptions are not verified regional occurrences or expert-certified diagnostic keys. Older dated conservation references are not current status assertions.

items.label: Adult sexual dimorphism
items.statement: Adult males are reported with pink facial skin and no black base on the bill; females resemble males in body plumage but have blue facial skin.
items.limitation: Sex-specific descriptions differ from other Penelopides. Facial skin color in the source set is not consistent across all publications.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Juvenile bill
items.statement: Juveniles resemble adults of the corresponding sex but show a smaller, smoother bill without adult striping.
items.limitation: Do not apply this character to an obscured or distant bill.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Forest and feeding context
items.statement: Described from primary and secondary rainforest, forest edges and agroforest containing fruiting trees. Fig and other fruit genera are recorded as resources.
items.limitation: The account reports records up to 1,000 m, not a universal upper occurrence limit.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Vocalization and grouping
items.statement: The account describes relatively deep calls and records observations in pairs and groups, with some groups reaching about twenty birds.
items.limitation: Sound transcription is descriptive, not a validated automated call classifier.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Published island range
items.statement: The cited specialist account places the species on Mindoro.
items.limitation: An island range summary does not verify presence at a surveyed point.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Global assessment reference
items.statement: The specialist account cites IUCN Endangered under criterion C2a(i), assessment year 2020.
items.limitation: This is an explicitly dated IUCN reference, not a current DENR Philippine legal listing.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindoro Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Adult male and female
items.statement: Male descriptions include a light head and underparts with darker upperparts and blue facial skin; females are predominantly dark with a pale-tipped tail.
items.limitation: Use sex-associated characters only after confirming age and viewing conditions.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Juvenile and subspecies caution
items.statement: Young birds can resemble the male but have smaller brown bills. The basilanicus form may lack the dark bill base seen in the typical form.
items.limitation: A single bill-base mark cannot establish identity across subspecies.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Forest and food
items.statement: Recorded in primary or secondary rainforest and forest edges, largely from lowland sites, feeding on fruit and seeds plus occasional animal material.
items.limitation: The cited account lists occurrences up to about 900 m, not a definitive absence above that altitude.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Calls and social behavior
items.statement: Calls are described as short and squeaky with varying pitch. Observations include pairs and groups of several birds.
items.limitation: Unreviewed auditory matches cannot establish a species identification.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Published distribution
items.statement: The cited account reports Mindanao and some adjacent smaller islands.
items.limitation: No provincial or GPS locality record is inferred from this reference.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Global assessment reference
items.statement: The specialist page cites IUCN Least Concern from the 2020 assessment.
items.limitation: Do not substitute this dated global category for Philippine DENR conservation status.
items.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group, Mindanao Hornbill account (cites IUCN 2020)

items.label: Dorsal color and pattern
items.statement: The cited diagnostic summary describes a dark back with small yellow specks on portions of individual scales.
items.limitation: Variation, lighting and image color balance limit visual comparison.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus mabitang account (Gaulke & Curio 2001 diagnosis)

items.label: Ventral and caudal scale texture
items.statement: The original comparative diagnosis describes strongly keeled ventrals and strongly keeled tail scales, unlike the smoother comparison recorded for V. olivaceus.
items.limitation: Scale texture needs a clear close view or suitable approved specimen evidence.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus mabitang account (Gaulke & Curio 2001 diagnosis)

items.label: Tree-associated natural history
items.statement: The source lists this monitor as arboreal and describes primarily plant-based feeding.
items.limitation: Do not convert a broad diet summary into a site-specific feeding observation.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus mabitang account (Gaulke & Curio 2001 diagnosis)

items.label: Island and type locality
items.statement: This source lists the species from Panay and gives a type locality near Pandan, Antique, around 250 m elevation.
items.limitation: Type-locality elevation is not the species' permissible altitude range.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus mabitang account (Gaulke & Curio 2001 diagnosis)

items.label: Published original description
items.statement: Species authority is Gaulke and Curio, 2001, with the original name Varanus mabitang.
items.limitation: Use the original publication for final diagnosis and taxonomic review.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus mabitang account (Gaulke & Curio 2001 diagnosis)

items.label: Dorsal comparison caution
items.statement: The comparative V. mabitang account describes V. olivaceus as greenish grey with darker crossbands.
items.limitation: Color alone does not establish the species; original diagnoses must be checked.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus olivaceus account

items.label: Rainforest and tree use
items.statement: The source records rainforest habitat and tree-associated activity, with fruit consumption noted in its dietary summary.
items.limitation: This does not imply that all rainforest sites support the species.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus olivaceus account

items.label: Published island distribution
items.statement: The account records southern Luzon, Polillo and Catanduanes. Its elevation figure describes known records.
items.limitation: Do not treat an upper observation figure as a modeled elevational exclusion.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus olivaceus account

items.label: Historical synonymy
items.statement: The account records older use of Varanus grayi alongside the currently accepted V. olivaceus.
items.limitation: Preserve the historically published name in original survey labels.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus olivaceus account

items.label: Reproduction
items.statement: The database lists oviparity for this species.
items.limitation: A taxon-level reproductive mode does not imply an observed breeding event.
items.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus olivaceus account
